title: A finitely presented factorization kills lifted product-comparison kernels
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $P,Q,T$ be $R$-modules, and let $a:P\to Q$, $b:P\to T$, $c:Q\to T$ be $R$-linear maps with $b=c\circ a$. Suppose $Q$ is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] and for every $R$-module $L$ one has $\ker(b\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)\subseteq\ker(a\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)$. For any set $A$ and family $(L_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}$ of $R$-modules, put $V=\prod_{\alpha\in A}L_\alpha$, with componentwise operations. Define $\theta_{T,(L_\alpha)}:T\otimes_RV\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}(T\otimes_RL_\alpha)$ by $t\otimes(\ell_\alpha)_\alpha\mapsto(t\otimes\ell_\alpha)_\alpha$. If $z\in P\otimes_RV$ satisfies $\theta_{T,(L_\alpha)}((b\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_V)(z))=0$, then $(a\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_V)(z)=0$ and $(b\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_V)(z)=0$. Tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Neither $P$ nor $T$ is assumed finitely presented or flat, and $A$ may be infinite or empty.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), proof of (1) implies (2), the three-row tensor/product diagram after choosing the dominating stage; extracted for arbitrary maps factoring through a finitely presented target.

proof.text: For each $\alpha\in A$ write $\pi_\alpha:V\to L_\alpha$ for the projection and put $z_\alpha=(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes\pi_\alpha)(z)$. For any module $M$, the map $\mathrm{id}_M\otimes\pi_\alpha$ is defined by the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], sending $m\otimes v$ to $m\otimes\pi_\alpha(v)$; it is the $\alpha$-coordinate of $\theta_{M,(L_\alpha)}$. For any linear $f:P\to M$, the identity $(\mathrm{id}_M\otimes\pi_\alpha)\circ(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)=(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{L_\alpha})\circ(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes\pi_\alpha)$ holds: both sides send $p\otimes v$ to $f(p)\otimes\pi_\alpha(v)$, and pure tensors generate. Apply this with $f=b$. The hypothesis that the comparison image is zero gives $(b\otimes\mathrm{id}_{L_\alpha})(z_\alpha)=0$ for every $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), proof (1) implies (2), commutativity of the three-row diagram and the coordinate kernels; Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property and pure-tensor generation.

proof.text: For each $\alpha$, apply the assumed kernel inclusion with the test module $L=L_\alpha$ to $z_\alpha$. Step 1 places it in $\ker(b\otimes\mathrm{id}_{L_\alpha})$, so $(a\otimes\mathrm{id}_{L_\alpha})(z_\alpha)=0$. Taking $f=a$ in the identity of Step 1 shows that these are exactly the coordinates of $\theta_{Q,(L_\alpha)}((a\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)(z))$. Hence that comparison image is zero, by equality of families coordinatewise.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), proof (1) implies (2), the sentence identifying product kernels using domination.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-presentation-tensor-products] with its finitely presented module $P$ replaced by our $Q$, and its family $(Q_\alpha)$ replaced by $(L_\alpha)$. Its comparison is exactly $\theta_{Q,(L_\alpha)}$, and is bijective, hence injective. Step 2 therefore gives $(a\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)(z)=0$, the first conclusion. The cited theorem allows arbitrary sets and arbitrary modules, so it imposes no finiteness on $A$ and no flatness on any $L_\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), proof (1) implies (2), injectivity of the bottom horizontal map supplied by Tag 059K (proposition-fp-tensor), (1) implies (2).

proof.text: Finally, the composition rule in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and $b=c\circ a$ give $(b\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)(z)=(c\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)((a\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)(z))=(c\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)(0)=0$. This is the second conclusion. If $A$ is empty, Step 2 still holds because two empty families agree, and Step 3 applies to the empty product; none of the steps chooses an index.
